summary: Mutual NDA on counterparty paper that is largely aligned with the playbook but adds a non-compete (2.4), an uncapped indemnity (7.1) and $100,000 per-breach liquidated damages (7.2).

findings.quote: The Receiving Party shall hold all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party in strict confidence
findings.why: Obligations and definitions use Disclosing/Receiving Party so either party can be either.

findings.quote: that is designated as confidential at the time of disclosure or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information or the circumstances surrounding disclosure.
findings.why: Marked or reasonably confidential information disclosed under the Agreement.

findings.quote: and shall use such Confidential Information solely to evaluate and perform the Purpose.
findings.why: Use is limited to the Purpose, a potential business relationship and technology collaboration.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or derive the composition, structure, or source code

the Receiving Party shall not, directly or indirectly, whether as principal, agent, partner, consultant, or otherwise, develop, market, distribute, license, or sell any software product, service, or feature that directly competes
findings.why: Imposes a non-compete and restriction on dealing with competitors for the term plus 12 months.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 2.4 in its entirety; nothing in this Agreement restricts either Party's business or its dealings with third parties.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept restrictions on either party's business in a confidentiality agreement; the confidentiality and non-use obligations already protect the information disclosed.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information only to those of its Representatives who need to know such information for the Purpose
findings.why: Need-to-know disclosure to Affiliates, officers, employees, counsel, accountants and advisors with liability for them; insurers are not named.

findings.quote: is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to, reliance upon, or use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present (3.2.1 to 3.2.4) with a written-proof standard.

findings.quote: to the extent legally permissible, provide the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice thereof
findings.why: Compelled disclosure permitted; notice only where legally permissible; cooperation at Disclosing Party's expense.

findings.quote: within fifteen (15) days of receipt of such request, securely destroy or return to the Disclosing Party all materials
findings.why: 15 days exceeds the 5 Business Day floor; 5.2 has the backup and statutory-retention exception.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information remains the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party.
findings.why: Ownership stays with the discloser and no licence is granted.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided on an "as is" and "with all faults" basis
findings.why: Mutual as-is disclaimer with no fraud exclusion.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Uncapped indemnity for any breach or alleged breach, contrary to the no-indemnity position.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 7.1; liability for breach is left to general law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not agree to indemnities in confidentiality agreements; each party remains liable for breach under general law.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall pay to the Disclosing Party, immediately upon written demand, the sum of one hundred thousand United States dollars ($100,000) for each such breach
findings.draft_redline: Delete the liquidated damages wording in 7.2; retain the acknowledgement of irreparable harm and mutual right to seek injunctive relief in 7.3.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We cannot agree to fixed per-breach payments; the mutual right to seek injunctive relief in clause 7.3 provides an adequate remedy.

findings.quote: each Party shall be entitled to seek immediate injunctive relief and specific performance, without posting bond or proving actual damages
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief, cumulative with other remedies.

findings.quote: for a term of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice
for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of such expiration or termination
findings.why: Three-year survival with indefinite protection limited to trade secrets.

findings.quote: the laws of England and Wales. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales
findings.why: English law and exclusive English jurisdiction.

findings.quote: This Agreement constitutes the complete and exclusive understanding between the Parties
findings.why: Customary entire-agreement clause with no fraud exclusion.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that either Party may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor entity
findings.why: Mutual consent requirement with a mutual successor exception, though no notice requirement.
findings.fallback_cited: Either party may assign to a Group member or successor on notice.
